newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 10.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- Four men and a woman were being quizzed on Wednesday after a major development in the Irish police investigation into the brutal murder of journalist Veronica Guerin.
- Soaring profits could speed up the privatisation of Irish state airline company Aer Lingus, the airline's chiefs said on Wednesday.
- The Irish government on Wednesday warned the social partners that looming industrial demands and disputes could mean a choice between pay rises or tax cuts.

- Almost 6,000 mobile phones were stolen in Ireland last year, affecting one in every 50 of the Eircell company's customers. - The Irish pound rose against continental currencies, as the dollar and sterling hit new peaks against the German mark. The Irish unit closed slightly down against the British currency.
- Ireland could easily slip back to the days of widespread industrial disputes and leapfrogging public sector pay claims, the leader of the main opposition party, Fianna Fail's Bertie Ahern, said.

- Relations between the Irish government and Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, have deteriorated sharply after the Irish Prime Minister, John Bruton, warned that a vote for the party in the Northern Ireland elections is a vote for the IRA's campaign of violence.
- A Dublin man is expected to appear in court on Friday on charges related to the murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin, who was shot dead in her car outside the city last June.

- Loyalist paramilitaries are believed to have been responsible for a gun attack on a Catholic in Belfast, Northern Ireland. - The Irish government has launched a 30 million Irish pounds project to have computers in every school by the year 2000.
- The German government is under strain as it tries to impose touch EMU conditions which Germany has difficulty qualifying for itself.

- A leak of lethal arsenic gas forced the evacuation of 150 staff from the National Microelectronics Research Centre in Cork on Wednesday, while across the road staff at a hospital knew nothing of the emergency.
- Ireland's Agriculture Minister, Ivan Yates, announced 64 new food industry jobs on Wednesday as part of an 8.7 million punts investment programme.
